main_text.p: ftatum peruenit: proinde intra quatuor & uiginti horas phlebotomia adminiftrandam effe fuadent peritiores practici. Vnde-'nam autem detrahendus fanguis fit nobis percunctari licet. Interdum incipit peftilens febris abfq; ullo bubone, aut carbunculo: interdum febrem antecedunt hi tumores praeter naturam.Idcirco si febris incipit abfq; illorum tumorum ullo detrahitur fanguis e uena interna finiftri cubiti (dum modo nulla adsit interna inflammatio, quę dolore, & alijs signis deprehendatur) propterea quod cor, & fplen omnium uiscerum maxime patiuntur: quemadmodum cardialgia, [illegible, ~9 letters], lipothymia, animi anguftia, triftitia, & metus, quorum non pauca peftilenti febre correptis adueniunt, fatis fuperq; reftantur. Quod si ob tenellam aetatem, aut uirium imbecillitatem cubiti uenam fecare non licet, tum natium partis finiftrae, uel cruri finiftro cucurbitulas cum fcarificatu affigemus, ut illa uidelicet uenenata materia ab his uiscerib. reuelli possit. Conferunt etiamnum hyrudines podicis uenis admotae, quae absq; ulla moleftia sanguinem uacuant. Caeterum si simul cum febre, aut ante febre appareat bubo, ftatim mittatur

page.notes: The Greek word between "cardialgia," and "lipothymia" is not legible at this scan resolution; it is marked as illegible. The large initial and the Greek are otherwise as printed. The catchword "mittatur" is taken from the foot and is not repeated in the text.
